title: Effective affine descents glue on invariant open neighbourhoods
statement: Let $p:X\to Y$ be finite, flat and surjective and $D$ a transport descent datum [def-pd-descent-datum] on $V\to X$. Suppose every point of $V$ has a transport-invariant affine neighbourhood $U$, contained in the inverse image of an affine open $B\subseteq Y$. Here invariant means that any test-scheme point whose image is in $U$ remains in $U$ after transport. Then $D$ is effective: there is $V_0\to Y$ and a transport-invariant projection $q:V\to V_0$ whose square over $p$ is cartesian [def-pc-base-change]. No finite-subset affine-neighbourhood hypothesis is used here.

source.place: Descent, Tags 0AP4 and 0245; Groupoid Schemes, proof of Tag 0H8K

proof.text: The neighbourhoods form an invariant open cover. Invariance in the reverse direction follows from inverse transport. Above each chosen affine B, the scheme X_B is affine because p is finite. Thus U to X_B is affine. Apply affine fpqc effectiveness to the restricted datum and view its descended model as a scheme over Y through B.

Intersections are invariant opens. Fpqc descent of opens identifies their models as open subschemes on both sides. Full faithfulness supplies unique transition isomorphisms and proves their cocycle. Scheme gluing gives V0 over Y; the local effective projections glue to q. Pullback and transport invariance hold locally on the cover, hence globally. Glue the empty cover to the empty Y-scheme when V is empty.

lean.statement: theorem isEffective_of_invariant_affine_neighbourhoods {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {p : X ⟶ Y} [IsFinite p] [Flat p] [Surjective p] {V : Over X} (D : Over.DescentDatum p V) (hcover : ∀ v : V.left, ∃ U : V.left.Opens, v ∈ U ∧ IsAffineOpen U ∧ (∃ B : Y.Opens, IsAffineOpen B ∧ U ≤ (V.hom ≫ p) ⁻¹ᵁ B) ∧ ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (f₁ f₂ : T ⟶ X) (h : f₁ ≫ p = f₂ ≫ p) (a : Over.mk f₁ ⟶ V), Set.range a.left ⊆ U → Set.range (D.transport f₁ f₂ h a).left ⊆ U) : D.IsEffective
